"""Text-to-SQL harness: draft -> execute/validate -> optional single repair call.

Contract (fixed): solve(task, env) -> {"sql": str}
  task  {"id", "db_id", "question", "hint"}
  env.chat(messages, max_tokens=None) -> str     policy calls capped at env.max_calls
  env.schema(db_id) -> str
  env.execute(sql, max_rows=20) -> dict          {ok, columns, rows, n_rows, error}
  env.descriptions(db_id) -> str
  env.prompt(name) -> str
  env.config -> dict
"""

import re

SQL_BLOCK = re.compile(r"```(?:sql|sqlite)?\s*(.*?)```", re.S | re.I)
LITERAL = re.compile(r"'((?:[^']|'')*)'")
IDENT = re.compile(r"\b([A-Za-z_][A-Za-z_0-9]*)\.([A-Za-z_][A-Za-z_0-9]*)\b")
BARE_CMP = re.compile(
    r"\b([A-Za-z_][A-Za-z_0-9]*)\s*(?:=|!=|<>|\bLIKE\b)\s*'((?:[^']|'')*)'", re.I
)
FROM_JOIN = re.compile(r"\b(?:FROM|JOIN)\s+([A-Za-z_][A-Za-z_0-9]*)(?:\s+(?:AS\s+)?([A-Za-z_][A-Za-z_0-9]*))?", re.I)
KEYWORDS = {
    "select", "from", "where", "join", "inner", "left", "right", "outer", "on",
    "group", "order", "by", "limit", "as", "and", "or", "not", "in", "is",
    "null", "like", "having", "union", "distinct", "case", "when", "then",
    "else", "end", "asc", "desc", "cross", "natural", "using", "offset",
}

SQL_WORDS = KEYWORDS | {
    "count", "sum", "avg", "min", "max", "cast", "coalesce", "ifnull", "nullif",
    "lower", "upper", "length", "substr", "substring", "trim", "ltrim", "rtrim",
    "replace", "round", "abs", "instr", "strftime", "julianday", "date", "time",
    "datetime", "exists", "between", "all", "any", "some", "with", "recursive",
    "intersect", "except", "values", "integer", "real", "text", "blob", "numeric",
    "varchar", "char", "float", "double", "boolean", "true", "false", "collate",
    "nocase", "glob", "escape", "over", "partition", "row_number", "rank",
    "dense_rank", "current_date", "current_time", "current_timestamp", "random",
    "total", "group_concat", "iif", "printf", "hex", "typeof", "last_insert_rowid",
}


def extract_sql(text):
    blocks = [b.strip() for b in SQL_BLOCK.findall(text or "") if b.strip()]
    if blocks:
        return blocks[-1].rstrip(";").strip()
    t = (text or "").strip()
    m = re.search(r"(?is)\b(select|with)\b.*", t)
    if m:
        t = m.group(0)
    return t.rstrip(";").strip()


def _safe_execute(env, sql, max_rows=20):
    try:
        r = env.execute(sql, max_rows=max_rows)
        if isinstance(r, dict):
            return r
    except Exception:
        pass
    return {"ok": False, "columns": [], "rows": [], "n_rows": 0, "error": "execution failed"}


def _table_aliases(sql):
    """alias/table-name -> real table name."""
    out = {}
    for tbl, alias in FROM_JOIN.findall(sql):
        if tbl.lower() in KEYWORDS:
            continue
        out[tbl.lower()] = tbl
        if alias and alias.lower() not in KEYWORDS:
            out[alias.lower()] = tbl
    return out


def _schema_columns(schema):
    """table -> [column names] parsed from CREATE statements (best effort)."""
    cols = {}
    for m in re.finditer(r"CREATE\s+TABLE\s+[`\"]?([A-Za-z_0-9]+)[`\"]?\s*\((.*?)\)\s*;", schema or "", re.S | re.I):
        tbl, body = m.group(1), m.group(2)
        names = []
        depth = 0
        cur = ""
        parts = []
        for ch in body:
            if ch == "(":
                depth += 1
            elif ch == ")":
                depth -= 1
            if ch == "," and depth == 0:
                parts.append(cur)
                cur = ""
            else:
                cur += ch
        parts.append(cur)
        for p in parts:
            p = p.strip()
            cm = re.match(r"[`\"]?([A-Za-z_][A-Za-z_0-9]*)[`\"]?", p)
            if cm and cm.group(1).lower() not in (
                "primary", "foreign", "unique", "check", "constraint", "key"
            ):
                names.append(cm.group(1))
        cols[tbl.lower()] = (tbl, names)
    return cols


def _literal_targets(sql, aliases, schema_cols):
    """Map each string literal to candidate (table, column) pairs."""
    targets = {}
    for m in BARE_CMP.finditer(sql):
        col, val = m.group(1), m.group(2)
        # qualified form immediately before?
        start = max(0, m.start() - 60)
        prefix = sql[start:m.start()]
        qm = re.search(r"([A-Za-z_][A-Za-z_0-9]*)\.$", prefix)
        cands = []
        if qm:
            tbl = aliases.get(qm.group(1).lower())
            if tbl:
                cands.append((tbl, col))
        if not cands:
            for tl, (tbl, names) in schema_cols.items():
                for n in names:
                    if n.lower() == col.lower():
                        cands.append((tbl, n))
        if cands:
            targets.setdefault(val, [])
            for c in cands:
                if c not in targets[val]:
                    targets[val].append(c)
    # literals used inside IN (...) lists
    for m in re.finditer(r"([A-Za-z_][A-Za-z_0-9]*(?:\.[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z_0-9]*)?)\s+IN\s*\(([^()]*?)\)", sql, re.I):
        colref, body = m.group(1), m.group(2)
        vals = LITERAL.findall(body)
        if not vals:
            continue
        if "." in colref:
            a, c = colref.split(".", 1)
            tbl = aliases.get(a.lower())
            cands = [(tbl, c)] if tbl else []
        else:
            cands = []
            for tl, (tbl, names) in schema_cols.items():
                for n in names:
                    if n.lower() == colref.lower():
                        cands.append((tbl, n))
        for v in vals:
            targets.setdefault(v, [])
            for c in cands:
                if c not in targets[v]:
                    targets[v].append(c)
    return targets


def _probe_values(env, sql, schema, budget):
    """For each string literal in the draft, show what the column really stores."""
    lits = [v for v in dict.fromkeys(LITERAL.findall(sql)) if v.strip()]
    if not lits:
        return [], budget
    aliases = _table_aliases(sql)
    schema_cols = _schema_columns(schema)
    targets = _literal_targets(sql, aliases, schema_cols)
    notes = []
    for val in lits:
        if budget <= 0:
            break
        cands = targets.get(val) or []
        core = re.sub(r"[%_]", "", val).strip()
        if not core:
            continue
        for tbl, col in cands[:2]:
            if budget <= 0:
                break
            frag = core.split()[0] if core.split() else core
            probe = (
                f'SELECT DISTINCT "{col}" FROM "{tbl}" '
                f"WHERE \"{col}\" LIKE '%{frag}%' LIMIT 8"
            )
            r = _safe_execute(env, probe, max_rows=8)
            budget -= 1
            if not r.get("ok"):
                continue
            vals = [row[0] for row in r.get("rows", []) if row]
            exact = any(isinstance(v, str) and v == val for v in vals)
            if exact and len(vals) == 1:
                continue
            shown = ", ".join(repr(v) for v in vals[:8]) if vals else "(no similar value found)"
            notes.append(
                f"- Column {tbl}.{col}: you filtered on {val!r}. Values actually stored that look related: {shown}."
            )
            break
    return notes, budget


def _probe_empty_join(env, sql, budget):
    """When a join returns nothing, show sample rows of the joined tables."""
    notes = []
    aliases = _table_aliases(sql)
    tables = list(dict.fromkeys(aliases.values()))
    if len(tables) < 2:
        return notes, budget
    for tbl in tables[:3]:
        if budget <= 0:
            break
        r = _safe_execute(env, f'SELECT * FROM "{tbl}" LIMIT 3', max_rows=3)
        budget -= 1
        if r.get("ok") and r.get("rows"):
            cols = ", ".join(str(c) for c in r.get("columns", []))
            rows = "; ".join(str(row) for row in r["rows"][:3])
            notes.append(f"- Sample rows of {tbl} ({cols}): {rows}")
    return notes, budget


def _static_diagnostics(sql, schema, question):
    """Schema-grounded checks that catch semantically wrong but executable drafts."""
    notes = []
    schema_cols = _schema_columns(schema)
    if not schema_cols:
        return notes
    aliases = _table_aliases(sql)
    all_names = set()
    for _, names in schema_cols.values():
        for n in names:
            all_names.add(n.lower())

    masked = LITERAL.sub("''", sql)

    # 1) identifiers that do not exist in the schema
    bad_tables = []   # tables whose columns we should show
    seen_bad = set()
    for m in IDENT.finditer(masked):
        a, c = m.group(1), m.group(2)
        al, cl = a.lower(), c.lower()
        if al in SQL_WORDS or cl in SQL_WORDS:
            continue
        tbl = aliases.get(al)
        if tbl is None:
            # maybe it is a real table name used directly
            if al in schema_cols:
                tbl = schema_cols[al][0]
            else:
                continue
        real_cols = schema_cols.get(tbl.lower(), (tbl, []))[1]
        if cl not in {x.lower() for x in real_cols}:
            key = (tbl.lower(), cl)
            if key in seen_bad:
                continue
            seen_bad.add(key)
            notes.append(
                f"- `{a}.{c}` does not exist: table {tbl} has columns {real_cols}. "
                "You likely invented a column name; use the real column names (check the foreign keys)."
            )
            bad_tables.append(tbl)

    # bare identifiers compared to literals / used after SELECT etc.
    for m in BARE_CMP.finditer(masked):
        col = m.group(1)
        cl = col.lower()
        if cl in SQL_WORDS or cl in all_names:
            continue
        # skip if it was part of a qualified reference already handled
        pre = masked[max(0, m.start() - 40):m.start()]
        if re.search(r"[A-Za-z_0-9]\.\s*$", pre):
            continue
        notes.append(
            f"- Column `{col}` does not appear anywhere in the schema. Use an existing column name."
        )

    # show real columns of tables involved when something was wrong
    if bad_tables:
        for tbl in dict.fromkeys(bad_tables):
            real = schema_cols.get(tbl.lower())
            if real:
                notes.append(f"- Actual columns of {real[0]}: {real[1]}")

    # 2) projection scope: entity-level question but only one name-like column selected
    q = (question or "").lower()
    entity_q = bool(re.search(r"\b(which|what|show|list|find|give)\b", q)) and not re.search(
        r"\bhow many\b|\bnumber of\b|\baverage\b|\bcount\b|\btotal\b|\bsum\b|\bmaximum\b|\bminimum\b|\bnames?\b|\bids?\b", q
    )
    sel_m = re.search(r"(?is)\bselect\s+(distinct\s+)?(.*?)\bfrom\b", masked)
    if entity_q and sel_m:
        proj = sel_m.group(2).strip()
        parts = [p.strip() for p in proj.split(",")]
        if len(parts) == 1 and "*" not in proj:
            p = parts[0]
            cm = re.match(r"(?:[A-Za-z_0-9]+\.)?[`\"]?([A-Za-z_][A-Za-z_0-9]*)[`\"]?$", p)
            if cm:
                cname = cm.group(1).lower()
                name_like = ("name" in cname or "title" in cname)
                joined = len(set(aliases.values())) >= 2
                details_q = bool(re.search(r"\bdetail|all the information|everything about\b", q))
                if (name_like and joined) or details_q:
                    notes.append(
                        "- Projection scope: the question asks about entities ('which/show ...'), not just a single attribute. "
                        "If it asks for the entities themselves or their details/all information, select the FULL rows of the main "
                        "entity table (e.g. `SELECT T1.*` or `SELECT *` including joined columns as the question implies), not only its name column."
                    )
    return notes


def _build_user(task, env, schema):
    user = f"Database: {task['db_id']}\n\nSchema:\n{schema}\n\nQuestion: {task['question']}"
    if task.get("hint"):
        user += f"\nHint: {task['hint']}"
    desc = ""
    try:
        desc = env.descriptions(task["db_id"]) or ""
    except Exception:
        desc = ""
    if desc.strip():
        user += "\n\nColumn descriptions:\n" + desc.strip()[:2000]
    return user


def solve(task, env):
    cfg = env.config or {}
    schema = env.schema(task["db_id"])
    system = env.prompt("system_prompt.md")
    user = _build_user(task, env, schema)
    messages = [
        {"role": "system", "content": system},
        {"role": "user", "content": user},
    ]
    reply = env.chat(messages, max_tokens=cfg.get("max_tokens", 800))
    sql = extract_sql(reply)
    if not sql:
        return {"sql": "SELECT 1"}
    if not cfg.get("enable_repair", True):
        return {"sql": sql}

    result = _safe_execute(env, sql)
    ok = bool(result.get("ok"))
    nrows = result.get("n_rows", 0) or 0
    err = result.get("error") or ""

    notes = []
    budget = int(cfg.get("max_probes", 6))
    needs_repair = False

    # static, schema-grounded diagnostics first (catch invented columns even when
    # the query executes fine, e.g. a subquery selecting a nonexistent column name
    # that SQLite resolves against an outer table, silently yielding wrong results)
    sn = _static_diagnostics(sql, schema, task.get("question", ""))
    if sn:
        needs_repair = True
        notes.extend(sn)

    if not ok:
        needs_repair = True
        notes.append(f"- Your query failed to execute. SQLite error: {err}")
    else:
        if nrows == 0:
            needs_repair = True
            notes.append("- Your query executed but returned ZERO rows. The question expects data, so a filter value, a join key or a condition is probably wrong.")
            if cfg.get("probe_zero_row_joins", True):
                jn, budget = _probe_empty_join(env, sql, budget)
                notes.extend(jn)
        if cfg.get("probe_literals", True):
            vn, budget = _probe_values(env, sql, schema, budget)
            if vn:
                needs_repair = True
                notes.extend(vn)

    if not needs_repair:
        return {"sql": sql}

    preview = ""
    if ok and nrows:
        preview = (
            f"\nCurrent result columns: {result.get('columns')}\n"
            f"First rows: {result.get('rows', [])[:5]}\n"
        )

    repair_user = (
        user
        + "\n\nYour previous query was:\n```sql\n" + sql + "\n```\n"
        + preview
        + "\nDiagnostics from checking it against the schema and running it on the real database:\n"
        + "\n".join(notes)
        + "\n\nWrite a corrected query. Use only column names that exist in the schema (the diagnostics above list the real ones); "
        "use the exact stored values shown above when they reveal a mismatch (casing, spacing, abbreviation); fix join keys using "
        "the schema's foreign keys; and make sure the selected columns match exactly what the question asks for (full rows of the "
        "main table when it asks for 'details'/all information about an entity, or for the entities themselves rather than a named "
        "attribute). Keep everything that was already correct. Return only the final query in one ```sql block."
    )
    try:
        reply2 = env.chat(
            [
                {"role": "system", "content": system},
                {"role": "user", "content": repair_user},
            ],
            max_tokens=cfg.get("repair_max_tokens", 700),
        )
    except Exception:
        return {"sql": sql}
    sql2 = extract_sql(reply2)
    if not sql2:
        return {"sql": sql}
    r2 = _safe_execute(env, sql2)
    if not r2.get("ok"):
        return {"sql": sql}
    if ok and nrows > 0 and (r2.get("n_rows", 0) or 0) == 0:
        return {"sql": sql}
    return {"sql": sql2}
